focus: Operator-added surface automation, external-user guide design, and adversarial review of rejected ideas X1-X9
noveltyJustification: Two newly verified command-contract boundaries and two partial refinements add evidence; the remaining findings re-evaluate prior rejections.
keyQuestions: Q10: R1-R4 stress test, what exact edit text and which files does each touch, what can still break, and is each the smallest correct fix?
Q11: What other hubs, tooling, CI, mirrors, catalogs, playbooks, batteries or release-engine rules assume the obsidian and webflow examples, and what does the end-to-end external-user flow hit?
Q12: Do the rejected ideas X1-X9 still hold, and which new ideas should be rejected?
answeredQuestions: Q12: Do the rejected ideas X1-X9 still hold, and which new ideas should be rejected?
ruledOut: A separate general-purpose sk-code surface wizard; extend the existing parent-skill command and document the bounded removal path.
A new doctor --fix surface migration branch; the release updater has a different unit and repair contract.

label: The existing /create:skill-parent command already scaffolds surface packets and updates the registry, router, leaf manifest, and parent-skill validation. This covers much of surface addition, but is only static contract evidence, not a successful add-surface run.

The create/update workflow says tieBreak must cover all modes, but does not say a newly added surface must precede sk-code-opencode. For an active root ROUTER.md it selects unchanged, so it does not prove that leaf maps are rebuilt.

/doctor:update handles release check, align, apply, rollback and compatibility actions. Its compiled-route follow-up refreshes the served manifest and reruns a guard, but does not name copying the refreshed manifest to the authored source path.

The external README still tells adopters to replace all three surfaces, including native OpenCode, while the sk-code README describes the three named surfaces as shared supported scope. A stack-adaptation guide should correct this at both entry points.
X1 remains rejected: a per-surface rank duplicates the explicit tieBreak order source and adds no demonstrated caller need.
X2 remains rejected: one native/fallback flag cannot order several user surfaces, and changing it risks the operator's existing example order.
X3 remains rejected: installed-packet presence does not encode preference among multiple surfaces; tieBreak already carries explicit precedence.
X4 remains rejected as a default: surfaceHint is applied after a route decision and only reorders matched surfaces, so callers without the hint still rely on tieBreak.
X5 remains rejected: removing example surfaces from the shipped operator tree is not equivalent to an external starter, and no publisher boundary was established in the prior synthesis.
X6 remains rejected: a separate operator/external config has no demonstrated consumer and duplicates the shipped tieBreak policy.

X7 remains rejected as a new guard: the parent-skill check already fails a registered mode whose packet directory is missing. That failure is not repair guidance, so the guide and doctor pointer remain necessary.

X8 needs narrowing: a second wizard is redundant because /create:skill-parent already accepts --surfaces, generates packets and leaf-manifest, and gates on parent-skill-check. The command contract does not document a complete removal operation or guarantee external-surface order.
X9 remains rejected: OpenCode detection is tied to resolved targets inside the hub's .skilled directory; putting it last would misroute genuine hub work in mixed-marker repositories.

Reject a separate general-purpose surface-management command for now. One existing command already owns package generation and validation; extending it and documenting the manual removal/re-mint path is cheaper, while no evidence shows a second caller or a distinct command contract is needed.
